headline: Daily research brief — Thursday, October 22

items.detail: Houthi strikes on Saudi targets Wednesday — one killed at Dammam civilian airport, two killed in a drone attack on a Saudi oil field — the US ordering diplomats and family members out of Saudi missions, and IRGC Navy strikes on four vessels plus mine collisions for three more west of Hormuz. Brent closed at $112.92 (+3.8%), a near-five-month high, and the Brent-WTI spread widened to $13.70 from $11.67: the market is pricing waterborne-supply risk specifically, not generic crude tightness. The inventory read is second-order — EIA's third straight crude draw (−3.1M bbl to 412.5M) was absorbed Wednesday morning with crude flat-to-down before the attacks. Natgas is balanced into winter: storage rose 77 Bcf to 3,644 Bcf, 4% below last year but 1% above the five-year average, leaving cold-snap upside intact. What would compress the premium: a verifiable US/Iran de-escalation signal, or next week's EIA flipping to a build with shipping normalized.
items.title: Middle-East escalation owns the macro tape; Brent at a near-five-month high

items.detail: The Oct-30 weekly straddle (mid $28.38 against $521.08) implies a ±5.45% move against an 8.09% four-quarter average reaction — the options market is pricing a tamer print than MSFT's own history suggests. The term structure agrees: the Oct-30 chain carries 44.15% ATM implied volatility against 21.73% on the Oct-26 pre-event chain, about 22 points of earnings premium sitting in the expiry that straddles Wednesday's report. Consensus is EPS $4.71 (14 estimates). The desk rule stands: premium into a binary event is to be avoided — no new short premium into the Oct-30 chain. What would change the read: an Azure or AI-capex guide-down, or a re-rating of the services-margin story on the call.
items.title: MSFT Oct 28 is the live binary — options price a tamer print than history

items.detail: Tesla reported Wednesday after the close; the stock fell 3.08% against a 5.95% four-quarter average move — a 'mixed, not bad' verdict. From the 8-K (Exhibit 99.1): GAAP net income of $787M fell 42.7% year on year and operating margin lost 322 basis points, with operating expenses up 39.2% as spending runs ahead of revenue. But operating cash flow held flat at $6.3B, free cash flow was $1.5B, cash and investments rose $1.9B quarter on quarter to $45.4B, and services-and-other posted record revenue of $4.6B (+32.5%) with record $734M gross profit — the quarter's margin resilience came from services mix, not autos. Implied volatility crushed as expected (76.76% to 39.50%), now only mildly rich against 33.6% trailing realized. Flag: Nasdaq records actual EPS at $0.20 against a $0.22 consensus, while the release itself states GAAP diluted EPS of $0.22 — UNVERIFIED, not resolved.
items.title: TSLA Q3 is sealed: mixed quarter, mild reaction, intact cash engine

items.detail: The FRED module ran clean today. The fed funds effective rate is 3.88% (the September hike passing through), the 2-year sits at 4.81% and the 10-year at 5.13%, with the 2s10s spread at 32 basis points — flattened from about 46 over the 60-day window but still upward-sloping. Funding markets are orderly: SOFR, EFFR and OBFR all print 3.88%, zero measurable stress. The policy picture is set: a Reuters poll of 100 economists has 94 expecting the FOMC to hold on Oct 27-28 at 3.75-4.00%, and all 100 expecting a December hike, after September CPI printed a hot 3.7%. With the 10-year above 5%, the discount-rate drag on long-duration growth multiples persists — a structural caution for writing rich calls against growth names on a rates-normalize thesis, not a signal to add premium. What would change it: an Oct 28 surprise or re-introduced guidance, a sub-3.5% CPI unwinding the December consensus, or 2s10s inversion.
items.title: Rates: front end pinned between a hot CPI and a quiet Fed
